turns.text: We have enough material for the issue, at least on paper. Could we tell the contributors we're going ahead with the evening launch?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: With the issue, yes. The evening is a different matter.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I thought the room had been reserved.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: A room has been held for us until Friday. Not necessarily that one, and not for the hours in the draft notice.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Right, so we can put the notice out without the time—

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I'd rather we didn't call it a launch notice yet. People might take the word launch as a promise that there will be an event.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Even if we say details to follow?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Especially if we say that. It suggests the event is settled and only the details remain. Could we let contributors know that the editorial work is continuing? They needn't hear about a venue at all.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: That would deal with the immediate message. It doesn't quite deal with the practical question, though. The evening option assumes one of the volunteers can stay late.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: I wouldn't rule it out on that account. We haven't actually asked.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Nor would I. I was objecting to treating the answer as already known, not to asking the question.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Then an internal enquiry about availability, separately from the contributors' update?

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Yes, that makes sense. And if the room is confirmed we can send the launch notice?

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Confirmed for the right hours, and with a volunteer. Even then, we'd need the editor to approve the event. I'm not the person who can give that permission.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Perhaps leave the notice out of today's action list. We can draft it privately, of course, but the action is to find out whether the evening is feasible.

turns.speaker: Nia
turns.text: Fair enough. I'll change the heading on our task list from “confirm launch” to “check evening option”. Does the contributor message still say we're going ahead?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: With editing, yes. I'd make the object explicit this time.

turns.speaker: Owen
turns.text: Agreed. We have enough material to continue editing. That's what we can say now.
